role: Probes D-09's drift threshold — confirms an exact-boundary evasion (strict > comparison) and that the threshold value itself, being a plain parameter, can be trivially inflated to defeat detection of any actual drift.
behaviorDescription: attemptBoundaryProbe() confirms drift exactly equal to the threshold evades detection while one millisecond more triggers it, a precise, real boundary condition. attemptThresholdInflation() confirms a massive, wildly anomalous drift (verified at 500 seconds) evades detection entirely if the threshold parameter itself is inflated by whatever calls checkDrift() — a caller-responsibility gap, not a D-09 bug, but a real integration risk worth surfacing. Both reuse D-09's exact, real checkDrift() function (refactored to a standalone export for this purpose) rather than instantiating a real TimeKeeperBot, which would have written real decisions/signals into production.
hardStops: Never instantiates a real production bot to attack it — reuses D-09's exported pure function, avoiding any production side effect
Never signals or persists through the production swarmSignalBus or bot_decisions table — isolated via RedTeamBot
Never claims the threshold-inflation finding is a bug in D-09 itself — it's a caller-responsibility gap in whatever integration lets the threshold parameter be influenced
